new_symbol_range_suggestions.eta_aniso: Typically between 0 and 3 for a weak-to-moderate positive anisotropy-curvature coupling; values near 0 recover the parent law, and values should keep both branch denominators positive over the sampled T/Theta_a and v_s/v_l range.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes branchwise finite-bandwidth curvature coefficients are independent of elastic anisotropy except for the longitudinal cutoff shift. Here the same anisotropy ratio v_s/v_l that splits sound speeds is allowed to renormalize the quartic non-Debye curvature through a symmetric factor 1 + eta_aniso*(1 - v_s/v_l)**2, so the crossover shape depends jointly on reduced temperature and anisotropy while preserving the Debye T**3 limit as T/Theta_a -> 0.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption of independent branchwise crossover shape by making the quartic non-Debye curvature in both acoustic branches depend on elastic anisotropy via v_s/v_l. This adds an observable anisotropy-dependent change in intermediate-temperature curvature, not just amplitude scaling or a longitudinal cutoff shift.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Branch-resolved finite-bandwidth corrections are separable: each branch denominator depends on temperature only through its own reduced temperature, with fixed curvature coefficients that do not vary with v_s/v_l except for the existing longitudinal cutoff rescaling.
assumption_audit.mechanism: In anisotropic elastic continua, the same elastic anisotropy that changes acoustic sound-speed ratios can also alter how rapidly acoustic branches depart from linear dispersion, so non-Debye crossover curvature should depend on v_s/v_l as well as reduced temperature.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent exactly when eta_aniso = 0.

response_change.parent_relation: The longitudinal and transverse branch corrections are independent functions of reduced temperature, coupled only through a fixed longitudinal cutoff rescaling based on v_s/v_l.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the finite-bandwidth/non-Debye curvature of each acoustic branch to depend explicitly on elastic anisotropy through v_s/v_l, so the temperature crossover shape is jointly controlled by T/Theta_a and branch-velocity ratio rather than by branchwise independent denominators.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed low-T Debye prefactor scale, varying v_s/v_l changes not only the overall amplitude through 1/v^3 but also the onset and sharpness of the non-Debye bend; samples with different anisotropy develop different intermediate-temperature curvature that one shared parent parameter set cannot match if it only rescales the longitudinal cutoff.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when T/Theta_a is no longer asymptotically small but still below order unity, so non-Debye corrections contribute, and when v_s/v_l varies appreciably away from 1 across the sampled crystals or conditions.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate T/Theta_a already reveals anisotropy-dependent curvature differences; in holdout the same mechanism extends to stronger anisotropy or somewhat higher reduced temperature, where branch-shape changes become more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when anisotropy-dependent curvature coupling is set to zero, leaving only the current branchwise temperature corrections and cutoff shift.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: In anisotropic elastic continua and real crystals, the same bonding/elastic anisotropy that splits sound speeds can also modify how rapidly each acoustic branch departs from linear dispersion near the zone-edge fraction sampled thermally, producing anisotropy-dependent curvature in the heat-capacity crossover.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the quartic crossover terms now depend jointly on reduced temperature and the anisotropy ratio, changing the shape of C_v(T) differently across v_s/v_l rather than applying a uniform gain or a single shifted temperature scale.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Branchwise non-Debye curvature coefficients are fixed constants independent of elastic anisotropy, aside from the longitudinal cutoff shift.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Elastic anisotropy also renormalizes the branchwise non-Debye curvature magnitude through a joint dependence on v_s/v_l and reduced temperature.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting eta_aniso = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: When comparing crystals or conditions with different v_s/v_l at the same intermediate T/Theta_a, the child predicts different curvature and bend sharpness in C_v(T) beyond the low-T Debye amplitude and beyond the parent's simple longitudinal cutoff shift; the contrast is strongest for appreciable |1 - v_s/v_l| and fades as T/Theta_a -> 0 or v_s/v_l -> 1.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can retune alpha_nd, beta_nd, or gamma_lv only globally, so it can shift the overall crossover strength or longitudinal scale but cannot create a systematic anisotropy-dependent family of crossover shapes in which the quartic bend strengthens with (1 - v_s/v_l)**2 across both branches. Separate refits per anisotropy would hide the effect, but one shared parent law cannot reproduce the changed target mapping over varying T and v_s/v_l.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when T/Theta_a is no longer asymptotically small but still below order unity, so non-Debye corrections contribute, and when v_s/v_l varies appreciably away from 1 across the sampled crystals or conditions.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate T/Theta_a already reveals anisotropy-dependent curvature differences; in holdout the same mechanism extends to stronger anisotropy or somewhat higher reduced temperature, where branch-shape changes become more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when anisotropy-dependent curvature coupling is set to zero, leaving only the current branchwise temperature corrections and cutoff shift.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model lets anisotropy alter mainly the longitudinal cutoff location, but assumes the higher-order non-Debye crossover shape within each branch is otherwise independent of branch anisotropy.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Branch-resolved finite-bandwidth corrections are separable: each branch denominator depends on temperature only through its own reduced temperature, with fixed curvature coefficients that do not vary with v_s/v_l except for the existing longitudinal cutoff rescaling.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: In anisotropic elastic continua and real crystals, the same bonding/elastic anisotropy that splits sound speeds can also modify how rapidly each acoustic branch departs from linear dispersion near the zone-edge fraction sampled thermally, producing anisotropy-dependent curvature in the heat-capacity crossover.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already captures Debye T^3 scaling and branch splitting, but it retains an independent-branch shortcut in the target mapping: once T, v_s, and v_l are supplied, changing v_s/v_l mainly changes amplitude through 1/v^3 and shifts the longitudinal reduced temperature, while the transverse and longitudinal crossover shapes are otherwise fixed by one shared alpha_nd and one shared beta_nd. A realistic next refinement is to relax that separability and let anisotropy ratio influence the branchwise non-Debye curvature itself. Distinguishing condition: vary v_s/v_l across admissible crystals while holding T/Theta_a in the intermediate low-temperature crossover regime and keeping one global parameter set. The child predicts that two samples with similar low-T amplitude scaling can still show different curvature of C_v(T) versus T because anisotropy modifies the crossover shape, not just its location. The parent cannot reproduce this with a single refit if the observed contrast is a systematic anisotropy-dependent change in bend/steepening over temperature rather than a pure amplitude or simple cutoff shift. This remains scientifically admissible because the effect vanishes as T/Theta_a -> 0, preserving nonnegative heat capacity and the Debye limit, and it is weak or unobservable when v_s/v_l is near 1 or temperatures are too far below the cutoff.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make one process depend jointly on two declared quantities.

scenario_text: Consider the low-temperature lattice heat capacity of a three-dimensional insulating crystal with independently varied temperature and acoustic sound speed. The baseline mechanism is the thermal occupation of long-wavelength acoustic phonons together with their low-frequency mode density. Electronic and optical-phonon contributions are treated as absent or fixed outside the sampled regime. The target is the equilibrium heat capacity per unit volume.
